solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet's wife, poetically, is blessed with technique

parts.note: hath is the old poetic form of has, to be blessed with
a way, as in a method or knack of doing something

explanation.surface: A literary note claiming the poet's wife, in verse, was gifted with real skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'hath a way': has a technique. Anne Hathaway was Shakespeare's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Hathaway married William Shakespeare, the poet par excellence, so she is literally the poet's wife.

clue.text: Hotel worker maybe interrupting while new person washed up

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a worker is a kind of bee, hence 'maybe'
as can mean while, at the same time that
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A hotel employee barges in on a newcomer who has just had a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: The bee sits between AS and N, after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is someone whose career or fame is over, just as a person washed up is finished.

clue.text: Formal garment with pleats, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: tucks are folds stitched into fabric, much like pleats

explanation.surface: A question about whether a formal outfit comes with pleats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tux is the informal short form of tuxedo, the dinner jacket worn on formal occasions.

clue.text: Chance one of those written on manuscript paper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: happening by luck, not by design

definitions.text: one of those written on manuscript paper
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a sharp, flat or natural sign written into music

explanation.surface: Musing on the odds of being one of the notes a composer jots down.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuscript paper is the ruled staff paper used for writing music, which is the clue to the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fortuitous and, in musical notation, a sign that alters a note's pitch.

clue.text: Old comedian almost getting head in order

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Bud Abbott, of the comedy double act Abbott and Costello

explanation.surface: A veteran funnyman nearly gets his life in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' here is a religious order, not tidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the superior of a monastery, the head of a community of a monastic order.

clue.text: Host in fluster finally donning skimpy outfit

indicators.note: donning is putting on clothing, so the outfit wraps round the letter

parts.note: a thong is a very skimpy item of swimwear or underwear

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word only

parts.note: the final letter of fluster

explanation.surface: A flustered party host ends up wearing something revealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like the person throwing the party; it means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can be a large crowd of people, which is exactly what a throng is.

clue.text: Almighty squeeze on income, ultimately

parts.note: a hug is an affectionate squeeze

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of income

explanation.surface: A news line about a massive squeeze on household earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Almighty is informal for enormous, as in an almighty row, so it is a synonym for huge.

clue.text: Exceptional — as work in relief?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a carving in relief literally projects from its background

explanation.walkthrough: Relief here is the sculptural sense, a design raised from a flat surface, not respite from pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means superlative, and also projecting from a surface, which is what a relief carving does.

clue.text: Continue through valley, please

indicators.note: going through something means passing inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
to add can mean to go on, as in 'he added that...'

explanation.surface: A polite request to keep going through the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'please' sits at the end like a courtesy, but it is the verb being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to make them happy, a close synonym of gladden as a transitive verb.

clue.text: Orang-utan briefly wrestled with legendary adventurer

indicators.note: wrestled suggests twisting and grappling, so the letters are thrown into a new order
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A tale of an ape grappling with a mythical hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts were the heroes who sailed with Jason on the Argo in search of the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Ten visiting Bucharest go twice around a house

indicators.note: visiting means the numeral for ten is staying inside the scrambled letters
around signals the letters of Bucharest and the doubled go are turned about into a new order
twice means go is written two times

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A party of ten touring Bucharest keeps circling round a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal and 'visiting' the container signal. The Saxe-Coburg-Gotha dynasty was Britain's royal house until 1917, when it was renamed Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house is a dynasty, and this German line was the name of Britain's royal family until 1917.

clue.text: Quest to find page in issue among the archives?

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other, here between two parts

parts.note: ex means former, describing something that now belongs in the archives
an issue of a newspaper or magazine is an edition
P is the standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A researcher hunts through old back issues for a particular page.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'ex-edition', a past issue, is what sits in the archives; the page goes between the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedition is a journey undertaken for a purpose, such as exploration, which is a quest.

clue.text: For example, king or queen in movie, original

parts.note: a picture is a film, as in 'going to the pictures'
a card is an eccentric or amusing person, an original

explanation.surface: A royal is cast in an inventive new film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King or queen' suggests royalty in a film; it means playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and jacks are the face cards in a pack, also called picture cards.

clue.text: Something on bottom of boot in farm

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a projecting ... on the sole of a football boot
second meaning: an establishment where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mud on a farm; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small knob on a boot sole for grip and a horse-breeding farm.

clue.text: Fizzy tonic water warmer when it's cold?

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sparkling mixer that somehow warms you up in chilly weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy coat worn in the cold season keeps the wearer warm, so it is a cold-weather warmer.

clue.text: Party without bottles? Don't ask me!

parts.note: without means having no
to can food is to preserve it, as one bottles it
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: Someone asked to throw a party with no drinks flatly refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole as a do with no can: a party lacking bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an idiom of refusal, a flat 'I can't help', much like 'Don't ask me!'

clue.text: Awfully unsettled after vacation and ever so tired

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters end up jumbled
vacating empties a place, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of unsettled
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone comes back from holiday feeling unsettled and utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired' is the hackneyed sense, as in a tired phrase, not sleepy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tired joke or phrase is stale from repetition, which is exactly what overused means.

clue.text: Indefinite number populating a northern Spanish city and northern French city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: populating a place means living inside it, so the letter goes within the city name

parts.note: Vigo is a port city in Galicia, north-west Spain
N is the standard abbreviation for northern
n is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A geography note pairing a city in northern Spain with one in northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'northern' is not part of the definition: it supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a city in Provence, in France, famous as the seat of the popes in the 14th century.

clue.text: Down in time, best coming earlier

parts.note: plum means choicest, as in a plum job
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A sporting phrase about a team going down when at their peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming earlier' puts the best piece before the time piece. 'Down' looks like a direction; it means soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the fine soft feathering of birds, and plumage is a bird's feathers collectively.

clue.text: Bird feeding fish to number of whales

indicators.note: food goes into a mouth, so feeding puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a pod is a group of whales or dolphins
char is a freshwater fish related to trout

explanation.surface: A seabird drops fish to a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck, a species of bird with a chestnut head in the male.

clue.text: Singers in empty theatre, it needing audio equipment brought in

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so these letters go into the others
an empty word has its inside gone, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: a mic is a microphone, audio equipment

explanation.surface: Performers in a deserted theatre need a microphone setup brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singers' suggests vocalists, but here they are songbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmice, or tits, are small songbirds, so they are singers in the bird sense.

clue.text: Big area has a little grandeur, as I anticipated

indicators.note: having a little of something means containing a piece of it, so the letters run across the words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of grandeur into anticipated

explanation.surface: A vast region turns out to be somewhat grand, just as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, the largest continental area on Earth.

clue.text: One removed from main cooker?

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of, so that letter is deleted

parts.note: chief means main or principal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A query about an oven taken off the electricity mains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooker' looks like an appliance; here it is a person who cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, and a cooker can be read as one who cooks.

clue.text: Shift gear, car failing to start — one probably not flying?

parts.note: to budge is to move or shift
rig means equipment or gear

indicators.note: failing to start means the beginning is missing, so the first letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver changes gear but the car will not start.
explanation.walkthrough: A budgerigar is normally kept caged as a pet, hence probably not flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Budgies are small parrots kept indoors in cages, so as birds they are probably not out flying.

clue.text: Artificial channel in position on the field

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man-made gutter or drain
second meaning: a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the off side

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, gully is a fielding position near the slips.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a drain or water channel and a close catching position in cricket.

clue.text: Broadcast live in the morning

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a.m. denotes the morning hours

explanation.surface: A programme goes out live on breakfast television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' looks like the broadcasting sense; it means exist.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam a programme is to transmit it by radio waves, so the verb means broadcast.

clue.text: Novel lament of Venus de Milo?

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the famous statue lost her arms, so her lament is a goodbye to them, and also a Hemingway title

explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo is an ancient Greek statue famously missing both arms; the title is Hemingway's 1929 war novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hemingway novel's title, read literally, is a goodbye to limbs, which the armless statue might well utter.

clue.text: Wife neglecting sandwich getting blame

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving out, so that letter is omitted

parts.note: a wrap is a sandwich made with a rolled flatbread
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife who forgets the lunch gets scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: The rap is informal for blame or punishment, as in to take the rap for something.

clue.text: Dead bird and mummy found in African capital

parts.note: the dodo is an extinct flightless bird, proverbially dead
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An extinct bird and an Egyptian-style mummy discovered in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mummy' hints at Egyptian tombs; it means mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodoma is the official capital city of Tanzania, in East Africa.

clue.text: Today's pie virtually ruined — miserable state

indicators.note: something ruined has been wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: virtually means almost entirely, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker laments that the day's pie is almost entirely spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dystopia is an imagined society of great suffering, the opposite of utopia, so a wretched state.
